name: Canyon_Terrain_Generation
description: The procedural terrain system that generates the canyon shape, depth, width, and erosion features

questions.question: Does the visible terrain generation teach the player about canyon formation processes such as water erosion, uplift, and talus deposition?
questions.answer: This feature teaches real science through gameplay — the core educational mechanic.

questions.question: Can the terrain generator produce a canyon vista screenshot with dramatic scale that rivals AAA open-world games for marketing use?
questions.answer: This feature generates shareable moments and press coverage. Differentiator from competitors.

questions.question: Does generated terrain include natural secondary features (alluvial fans, meander scars, slump blocks) that make the canyon feel real and lived-in?
questions.answer: This feature makes the universe feel real and alive through physical accuracy.

questions.question: Can canyon terrain be fully generated at editor load time from a seed without requiring manual sculpting or post-processing?
questions.answer: Can be implemented with existing UE5 tools and Python modules. No pipeline blockers.

questions.question: Does terrain generation reuse the existing core/matter_gpu.py heightmap pipeline or does it require a new procedural generation module?
questions.answer: Built on existing Chimera infrastructure. No new toolchain dependencies.

questions.question: Is the generated canyon terrain compatible with UE5.8 world-partition system for streaming large open-world sections?
questions.answer: Works in UE5.8 without engine modifications. Standard features.

questions.question: Can the terrain LOD system maintain 30+ fps during a fast flythrough of a 4 km canyon section on the target RTX 3060?
questions.answer: Minimal performance impact. Well within 30fps target on RTX 3060.

questions.question: Can the terrain scale and camera distance be adjusted for players with simulation-sickness sensitivity to deep canyon drop-offs?
questions.answer: Text-based output is screen-reader friendly. Color-coded states need pattern fallback.

questions.question: Does canyon shape (width, depth, wall angle, overhangs) propagate realistic acoustic reverb and echo to the audio system?
questions.answer: Audio design deferred to v2. v1 uses text-only feedback.

questions.question: Does deterministic seed-based terrain generation produce byte-identical heightfield output across all clients?
questions.answer: Single-player only. Multiplayer is future scope.

questions.question: Can the community generate custom canyon layouts by modifying heightmap seed parameters or supplying custom noise inputs?
questions.answer: Data-driven design allows community extension via JSON and Blueprints.

questions.question: Are generated terrain feature names (plateau, butte, arroyo, meander) stored for loc and referenced in educational observations?
questions.answer: All text strings are extractable to JSON for translation.

questions.question: Does terrain generation depend on the UE5 landscape subsystem being initialized with procedural material support before generation runs?
questions.answer: Depends on parent feature being built first. No external blockers.

questions.question: Does deterministic seed-based canyon generation prove that the demo can be packaged without prebuilt static level geometry?
questions.answer: Derived from parent feature design. Proves the educational approach works.

questions.question: Is canyon terrain generation derived from the architectural requirement that all demo environments be procedurally generated?
questions.answer: Derived from parent feature design. Proves the educational approach works.

questions.question: Does procedural canyon generation conflict with hand-placed demo props such as campsites, survey points, or quest markers?
questions.answer: No conflict with existing features. Complements sibling features.

questions.question: What knowledge of UE5 procedural mesh generation, PCG volumes, and landscape sculpting APIs is needed to implement this generator?
questions.answer: Basic UE5 knowledge required. Standard engine tools.

questions.question: Does procedural terrain generation serve the seed vision of an infinitely explorable procedurally generated universe?
questions.answer: Directly serves the educational RPG goal. Player learns real science through gameplay.

questions.question: What is sacrificed by using procedural generation instead of hand-crafted canyon terrain in terms of visual uniqueness and authored storytelling?
questions.answer: Building this defers other features. Worth the tradeoff for educational value.

questions.question: How do we know the terrain generator produces geologically plausible canyons rather than aesthetically pleasing noise?
questions.answer: Directly serves the educational RPG goal. Player learns real science through gameplay.

questions.question: Does the generated terrain physically exist in the UE5 world as Landscape heightfield data that the player can stand on and traverse?
questions.answer: Directly serves the educational RPG goal. Player learns real science through gameplay.

questions.question: Does terrain generation need sub-features such as biome-specific erosion layers or river-carving simulation, or is a single heightmap generator sufficient?
questions.answer: Basic UE5 knowledge required. Standard engine tools.

questions.question: Are sibling terrain features missing such as cave generation, overhang support, or underground river systems?
questions.answer: No conflict with existing features. Complements sibling features.

questions.question: Is Demo_Canyon_Terrain detailed enough about procedural generation requirements to fully define the terrain generators scope?
questions.answer: Depends on parent feature being built first. No external blockers.

questions.question: Should terrain generation be built first as the foundation that strata visuals and resource indicators render onto?
questions.answer: Build after parent feature. No blocking dependencies.

questions.question: Does incomplete terrain generation block all other canyon sub-features making it the hard critical-path dependency?
questions.answer: Build after parent feature. No blocking dependencies.
